subject: Ted Lieu isn’t lying — he’s telling you half the story
posts:
A masterclass in selective history. Rep. Ted Lieu's arguments rely on true facts, but omit the crucial context that complicates them.
Evidence: Historical accuracy, Selective omission, Partisan framing
#Aletheia #USPol 🌐

The claim is that Rep. Ted Lieu is a transparent truth-teller whose arguments are built on solid, unassailable facts, even if they present a simplified version of history.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +0.2) — Good Preference

In reality, selective omission is a form of deception. By leaving out complicating historical context, the actor constructs a convenient narrative to maximize partisan advantage.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.35, +0.45) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Deception. The actor uses accurate individual facts as a pretext to construct a highly partisan, incomplete historical narrative.
Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 0.88, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Ted Lieu: FAIL (-0.35, 0.45) — Uses selective facts to spin history.
- Washington Examiner: COND (0.1, -0.2) — Highlights omission but with partisan framing.
Rep. Ted Lieu (D-CA) is criticized for presenting selective historical facts to support his political arguments, omitting the broader, more complex context that might challenge his narrative.

The Bright Side:
Highlighting these omissions encourages voters to seek out the full, complicated history rather than accepting simplified partisan talking points.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is confusing the truth of individual facts (WHAT) with the honesty of the overall narrative (WHY). A collection of true facts can still construct a false picture when key context is suppressed.

Social Physics Analysis:
Lieu executes a Smart Selfish Maneuver. He uses the pretext of factual accuracy to hoard narrative power, projecting a false sense of transparency while actively avoiding the empathy required to address complex historical realities.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Deception.
When you map the gap between stated facts and omitted context, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The systemic gravity of selective truth-telling pulls public discourse into deeper polarization.

The Unavoidable Truth: Ted Lieu uses accurate individual facts to build his political arguments.
The Unavoidable Lie: Omitting historical context that complicates the narrative is still honest communication.

Alethekanon:
Selective omission is the preferred currency of partisan rhetoric. By presenting only the facts that serve the narrative, actors construct a fragile reality that collapses under historical scrutiny.

Awwthekanon:
It's sad when leaders feel they have to hide parts of our shared history just to win an argument. We deserve the whole truth, even when it's complicated, so we can heal together.

Brothekanon:
Bro, cherry-picking history is classic. Just tell us the whole story and let us decide. Omit the context and you're basically just spinning a yarn.

Spirithekanon:
"He who speaks truth declares righteousness, but a false witness, deceit." Proverbs 12:17 FAIL
Presenting half-truths to win a debate is merely a decorated form of deception.
